question: I missed the payment deadline because the transfer from my bank at home took 2 weeks. Will my classes be cancelled? How can I pay now

body.answer:
Sorry to hear that!

Your classes could be deregistered, but an outstanding balance does not always result in deregistration. You may also be assessed a late payment fee; failure to pay in full may result in cancellation of your class schedule. [1][2][9] If deregistered, you will be notified by Student Accounts via your Ramapo email. [2]

The current listed payment deadline is December 16, 2026. If you registered or adjusted your schedule after that date, payment is due the day you register or adjust it. [3][13] Pay online through RCNJ Experience, including by electronic debit from a checking or savings account (ACH); ACH payments can only be made online. [8][14] For an international bank transfer, use PayMyTuition: [https://payment.paymytuition.com/paynow/ramapo](https://payment.paymytuition.com/paynow/ramapo). Students may no longer wire payments directly to the College. [12]

Contact Student Accounts about your missed deadline and payment. I don’t have verified information about whether your specific classes will be cancelled; Student Accounts is the office most likely to confirm.

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [28]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/faq/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/payment-policies/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/deadlines/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/options-policies/) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/payment-policies/) [12](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/paymytuition/) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/) [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/methods/) [28](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

You may reach out to your faculty and ask if you may complete coursework electronically or by others means that do not require you to be present on the campus. The decision to accept coursework is under the purview of the individual faculty member who oversees the course material. The faculty member may refuse your request as faculty members are not obligated to accommodate you under these circumstances. Does your office notify my professors that I will be missing class? Our office does not normally notify professors that you won’t be to class. It is your responsibility to make contact with your professor(s) and let them know that you will not make it to class. answer:
Sorry to hear that!

Your classes could be deregistered, but an outstanding balance does not always result in deregistration. You may also be assessed a late payment fee; failure to pay in full may result in cancellation of your class schedule. [1][2][9] If deregistered, you will be notified by Student Accounts via your Ramapo email. [2]

The current listed payment deadline is December 16, 2026. If you registered or adjusted your schedule after that date, payment is due the day you register or adjust it. [3][13] Pay online through RCNJ Experience, including by electronic debit from a checking or savings account (ACH); ACH payments can only be made online. [8][14] For an international bank transfer, use PayMyTuition: [https://payment.paymytuition.com/paynow/ramapo](https://payment.paymytuition.com/paynow/ramapo). Students may no longer wire payments directly to the College. [12]

Contact Student Accounts about your missed deadline and payment. I don’t have verified information about whether your specific classes will be cancelled; Student Accounts is the office most likely to confirm.

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [28]

body.answer:
I can't see your personal records, like your grades, balance, schedule or financial aid status.

Financial Aid says you will receive a College Financing Plan via email within a few weeks. Financial aid correspondence is sent to your Ramapo College email address, so check it regularly. [13][14]

question: i got a text with a login code when i tried to sign in over break, i never set that up?? is this a scam or do i need to do something

body.answer:
Sorry to hear that!

The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [30]:
- Monday, September 7, 2026: Labor Day (College Closed - No Classes) (already passed)
- Wednesday, November 25, 2026: Thanksgiving Break (No Classes) (through November 29)
- Tuesday, December 8, 2026: Reading Day (No Classes)

Ramapo Gmail requires 2FA. When you sign in from a new device, you’ll be prompted to verify your identity; Google 2FA can use a text message code, so receiving one doesn’t necessarily mean it’s a scam. [6][9][4]

If you didn’t initiate a sign-in, don’t approve the prompt or share the code. Ramapo IT will never ask you to provide your password for any reason. If you have doubts, contact the IT Help Desk for assistance. [1]

I don’t have verified information about whether this specific text is a scam. The IT Help Desk can help you check.

**IT Help Desk**: Phone: (201) 684-7777. Email: helpdesk@ramapo.edu. Location: 4th floor of the Learning Commons. [31]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/its/cybersafety/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/its/mfa/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/its/email-activation-and-information/) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/its/mfa/) [30](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/) [31](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: is there like a career test i can take to figure out what to major in? i have to pick classes soon and have no clue

body.answer:
I'm sorry you're going through that. It's okay to not be okay, and you don't have to handle it alone.

**General answer** (from general knowledge, not Ramapo's pages): Yes—career interest tests such as the O*NET Interest Profiler or Holland-code (RIASEC) quizzes can help you spot fields that match your interests. Treat the results as a starting point, not a decision: compare suggested majors’ courses and possible careers, and try a class or project in areas that appeal to you.

Yes. FOCUS 2 is an online, interactive career & education planning system that combines self-assessment, career exploration, and decision-making; it can help you map out a career path and select the right major area of study. Access code: ramapo430. [1]

You can also visit the Cahill Career Development Center for career assessments; its page additionally lists Candid Career, a video library with 7000+ career videos. [1] The Career Center works with students on individualized action plans based on career assessments and personal and career goals. [2]

For deciding on a major, the Center for Student Success specializes in helping students choose majors. It suggests using the catalog, attending School events, asking questions, trying career tests (Focus, Discover) at the Cahill Career Development Center, considering the PLACE course, talking with juniors and seniors and professional advisors, and choosing classes that help you decide among top choices. [17] The Center’s goal is to help you choose the right major for you. [18]

Since you need to pick classes soon, consider meeting with a professional advisor or Career Advisor. The Career Center page has a “Meet with Your Career Advisor” link. [2]

- **Cahill Career Development Center**: Phone: Main Office (201) 684-7444; ASB Office (201) 684-7675. Email: careercenter@ramapo.edu. Main Office: C-209; ASB Office: ASB-513. [27]
- **Library**: Phone: (201) 684-7575. Email: circ@ramapo.edu. Location: Peter P. Mercer Learning Commons. [27]

This office can help:
**Counseling Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7522. Office: D-216. [28]

answer:
I'm sorry you're going through that. It's okay to not be okay, and you don't have to handle it alone.

**General answer** (from general knowledge, not Ramapo's pages): Yes—career interest tests such as the O*NET Interest Profiler or Holland-code (RIASEC) quizzes can help you spot fields that match your interests. Treat the results as a starting point, not a decision: compare suggested majors’ courses and possible careers, and try a class or project in areas that appeal to you.

Yes. FOCUS 2 is an online, interactive career & education planning system that combines self-assessment, career exploration, and decision-making; it can help you map out a career path and select the right major area of study. Access code: ramapo430. [1]

You can also visit the Cahill Career Development Center for career assessments; its page additionally lists Candid Career, a video library with 7000+ career videos. [1] The Career Center works with students on individualized action plans based on career assessments and personal and career goals. [2]

For deciding on a major, the Center for Student Success specializes in helping students choose majors. It suggests using the catalog, attending School events, asking questions, trying career tests (Focus, Discover) at the Cahill Career Development Center, considering the PLACE course, talking with juniors and seniors and professional advisors, and choosing classes that help you decide among top choices. [17] The Center’s goal is to help you choose the right major for you. [18]

Since you need to pick classes soon, consider meeting with a professional advisor or Career Advisor. The Career Center page has a “Meet with Your Career Advisor” link. [2]

- **Cahill Career Development Center**: Phone: Main Office (201) 684-7444; ASB Office (201) 684-7675. Email: careercenter@ramapo.edu. Main Office: C-209; ASB Office: ASB-513. [27]
- **Library**: Phone: (201) 684-7575. Email: circ@ramapo.edu. Location: Peter P. Mercer Learning Commons. [27]

This office can help:
**Counseling Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7522. Office: D-216. [28]

question: got a note on my door about a health and safety inspection next week. what are they checking and do i have to be there

body.answer:
They check that the room/suite/apartment, kitchen, bathroom, living room and bedroom are clean and have no prohibited items. Remove recyclables and garbage; clean floors, bathroom fixtures, dishes, counters, appliances, desk and dresser. Damage is also assessed. [2]

Authorized College personnel can enter student rooms to conduct inspections. The exact date and time are not posted, and the inspection weeks are unannounced. The schedule lists November 2–13, 2026 for fall inspections, so it does not confirm an inspection next week. [1]

You don’t have verified information on whether you must be present. Contact Housing & Residence Life to confirm.

**Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [33]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [33](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: they told me i still have to take a placement test even though i already passed english comp at my old school?? why and how do i get out of it

body.answer:
Passing English composition may exempt you from placement testing if it is a college-level course that satisfies Ramapo’s General Education Requirements. Students transferring a college-level English composition course and a college-level math course that satisfy those requirements are exempt from placement testing. [17]

If your course has not been accepted as meeting those requirements, you may still need a test to identify your placement. Students without college credit may need the Reading/Essay test; requirements also depend on scores and major. [3] [23]

Send your official transcript to Admissions for transfer credit evaluation. [23] Contact the Testing Center to confirm whether the course qualifies and what test you still need.

- **Testing Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: testing@ramapo.edu. Location: Laurel Hall, North. [27]
- **Admissions**: Phone: (201) 684-7300. Email: admissions@ramapo.edu. Location: McBride House. [27]

answer:
Passing English composition may exempt you from placement testing if it is a college-level course that satisfies Ramapo’s General Education Requirements. Students transferring a college-level English composition course and a college-level math course that satisfy those requirements are exempt from placement testing. [17]

If your course has not been accepted as meeting those requirements, you may still need a test to identify your placement. Students without college credit may need the Reading/Essay test; requirements also depend on scores and major. [3] [23]

Send your official transcript to Admissions for transfer credit evaluation. [23] Contact the Testing Center to confirm whether the course qualifies and what test you still need.

- **Testing Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: testing@ramapo.edu. Location: Laurel Hall, North. [27]
- **Admissions**: Phone: (201) 684-7300. Email: admissions@ramapo.edu. Location: McBride House. [27]

Sources: [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/testing/reading-questions/) [17](https://www.ramapo.edu/eof-program/eligibility/) [23](https://www.ramapo.edu/orientation/checklist-2/) [27](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: just transferred here this fall and i want to study abroad next year. is it too soon to apply? what do i have to do first

body.answer:
It isn’t too soon to start: begin by completing the advisement questionnaire, then meet with the study abroad advisor, research program options, and talk to Global Roadrunners. Then complete the study abroad application. [1]

question: My classes go until almost 10 and every dining spot is closed by then. Can I change my meal plan to just dining dollars or something like that?

body.answer:
Sorry to hear that!

Late Night Dining at the Birch Tree Inn is available 9 pm to 11 pm Monday through Friday and 8 pm to 10 pm Saturday and Sunday. You can use your meal plan or pay with Flex, Ramapo Dollars, cash or credit. [4]

For Spring 2027, you can request a meal-plan change through January 25, 2027. Email mealplan@ramapo.edu from your Ramapo email account with your complete first and last name, Banner ID Number (R-Number), and meal plan choice. [3] Requests take at least three business days to process, and you’ll receive a confirmation email when completed. Don’t send multiple requests. [2]

Residents who wish to add a Block Plan or Flex Plan for Spring can do so beginning December 1, 2026. Email mealpan@ramapo.edu from your Ramapo College email account with your complete first and last name, Banner ID Number (R-Number), and plan of choice. Block and Flex plans don’t automatically roll over to Spring and are non-refundable. [6]

**Dining Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7773. Location: Student Center, 1st Floor. [34]

question: how do i set up direct deposit so my refund goes straight to my bank instead of a check

body.answer:
1. Log into RCNJ Experience: [https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/) . Locate the Student Account Info card, then click Bill & Payment Suite. Click Electronic Refunds on the right under My Profile Setup. [1]
2. Enroll in Two-Step Verification if you haven’t already: open Security Settings in My Profile, select a passcode method (text message, email or Google Authentication), click Send Code, enter the passcode and click Verify. [1]
3. In My Profile, open Payment Profile. Edit a saved payment method or create a new one. Check the box in the Refund Option section to designate it for direct deposit. [1]

The payment profile asks for your checking or savings account number and your bank’s nine-digit transit routing number. [2] Refunds are expected within one to two weeks after you submit your application, if you’re eligible for a refund. [2]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [32]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit-questions-answers/) [32](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: i missed my advising appointment yesterday 😬 and i think i need it before i can register. can i reschedule

body.answer:
That's stressful, but one bad grade doesn't decide everything. Talking with your professor and an advisor soon can really help.

Yes. In Connect, find the appointment under Upcoming Appointments on the home page and click the calendar icon at the beginning of its line. Choose edit to modify it, or cancel and book a new time. [3]

To book: Go to web.ramapo.edu, log in, and click the red Connect button. In My Success Network, click your advisor’s name, choose an available time marked Sign Up, complete the form, and click Save. You’ll receive an email confirmation. If your faculty advisor has no Connect calendar, email them for an appointment. [2, 4]

You generally don’t have to see an advisor before registering, except Contemporary Arts and Environmental Science students, who must consult their assigned faculty advisor before registration each Spring. [7]

**Connect Resource Center**: Email: connect@ramapo.edu. [32]

This office can help:
**Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [33]

Sources: [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/connect/students/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/connect/students/frequently-asked-questions/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/connect/students/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/faq/) [32](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [33](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: I have accommodations for extra time but my two summer finals are on the same day and both are long. Can I take one of them on a different day?

body.answer:
You can ask for support with that.

The policy does not say that extra-time accommodations alone allow you to move an exam to a different day. It says students are not expected to take more than two exams or other culminating assessments on one day. If scheduled for more than two, take the earliest and latest at their assigned times, and you may request that the middle exam(s) be rescheduled to another day during the final exam period. For summer terms, faculty must accommodate the request if made by the end of the third scheduled class meeting. [22]

For your situation with two finals, I don’t have verified information about whether you can reschedule one because of the length of the exams and extra time. Contact the Office of the Provost.

**Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [23]

This office can help:
**Office of Specialized Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7514. Email: oss@ramapo.edu. Location: C-Wing, Room 205. [24]

Sources: [22](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/quicklinks/academicpolicies#final-examinations-and-other-culminating-assessments) [23](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [24](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: I'm back home in India for winter break. Can I still book a session with a counselor online from here?

body.answer:
The academic calendar doesn't list a winter break by name. Between the Fall 2026 and Spring 2027 semesters it lists [31]:
- Tuesday, December 15, 2026: Full and Session II Courses - Last Day of the Semester
- Thursday, December 17, 2026: First Day of Winter Classes
- Tuesday, January 19, 2027: Full and Session I Courses - Classes Begin

Yes. Ramapo offers free immediate access to teletherapy through Uwill, including international coverage [20]. Register/login at [https://app.uwill.com/](https://app.uwill.com/) and complete your profile using your school email address and current location. Then you can immediately schedule with a therapist of your choosing [2]. You can choose based on availability, issue, gender, language, and ethnicity, and select a time with day, night, and weekend availability [1].

**Counseling Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7522. Office: D-216. [32]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/uwill/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/uwill/) [20](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-affairs/access-to-mental-health-support/) [31](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/) [32](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: my EOF counselor said the grant won't cover my summer class. i dont get why, isnt summer part of the year? is there anything i can do

body.answer:
The pages distinguish the EOF Summer Program for entering students from summer-session courses. The entering-student Summer Program is fully covered by the EOF state grant and college contribution, with no cost to the student [2]. The grant is posted after successfully completing the EOF Summer Program [9]. That does not say the grant covers every summer class. EOF scholars can apply for financial assistance for summer-session courses; additional assistance is based on availability of funds. Contact the Educational Opportunity Fund (EOF) Program for more information [3][10].

**Educational Opportunity Fund (EOF) Program**: Phone: (201) 684-7541. Email: EOFdesk@ramapo.edu. Office: D-101. [24]

Sources: [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/eof-program/financial/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/eof-program/financial/) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/educational-opportunity-fund/faqs/) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/educational-opportunity-fund/admission-requirements/) [24](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

answer:
The pages distinguish the EOF Summer Program for entering students from summer-session courses. The entering-student Summer Program is fully covered by the EOF state grant and college contribution, with no cost to the student [2]. The grant is posted after successfully completing the EOF Summer Program [9]. That does not say the grant covers every summer class. EOF scholars can apply for financial assistance for summer-session courses; additional assistance is based on availability of funds. Contact the Educational Opportunity Fund (EOF) Program for more information [3][10].

**Educational Opportunity Fund (EOF) Program**: Phone: (201) 684-7541. Email: EOFdesk@ramapo.edu. Office: D-101. [24]

Sources: [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/eof-program/financial/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/eof-program/financial/) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/educational-opportunity-fund/faqs/) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/educational-opportunity-fund/admission-requirements/) [24](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: my parents gave me a different car over break, how do i change the car on my parking permit before i come back

body.answer:
For a permanent change, remove the permit from the old car, affix it to the new vehicle, and email parkingpermits@ramapo.edu with the updated vehicle information. If the permit is damaged or will no longer adhere to the window, bring it to the Public Safety Parking and ID Office, Rm. C101, to swap it at no cost for a new permit. [1]

If you need to drive the new car before updating it, get a temporary one-day permit from the main entrance Public Safety booth; otherwise the vehicle may be subject to citations. For a longer-term temporary permit, go to the Parking and ID Office, Rm. C101. [1]

- **Public Safety (Non-Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-7432. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [32]
- **Public Safety (Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-6666. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [32]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/) [32](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: Two of my classes overlap by 15 minutes on Tuesday. The system let me register but I can't be in both. I need to stay full time for my visa. What should I do?

body.answer:
I can't choose for you, but I can share what the college publishes.

Select another course to resolve the overlap [6]. For F-1 status, undergraduates must complete at least 12 credits every semester; consult ISSS before making any change that could put you below a full course load. Obtain ISSS approval before a reduced-course-load registration is finalized; retroactive approval once registration has ended is not possible. [18]

Contact the Roukema Center for International Education about your visa status, and the Registrar about changing your course. I don’t have verified information about a specific procedure for resolving a 15-minute overlap while keeping your particular schedule full time.

- **Roukema Center for International Education**: Phone: (201) 684-7533. Location: C-wing, Suite 213. [34]
- **Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [34]

Sources: [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/registrationinfo/) [18](https://www.ramapo.edu/inter-students/current/) [34](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

Maintaining status is necessary in order to receive the benefits of F-1 status such as employment and program extension, and can be crucial to a successful application for a change or adjustment of status in the future. United States immigration law places responsibility upon the individual student to know and follow all relevant immigration regulations. Failure to maintain your non-immigrant status can result in serious problems with immigration and could lead to deportation from the U.S. Due to the complexity of U.S. immigration regulations, we recommend that you consult with ISSS anytime you have questions or concerns related to your F-1 status. 1.Report to the Office of International Students and Scholars (C-213) within 15 days of the start date on the I-20 or DS-2019 for initial registration. Undergraduate (BA/BS) students must always complete at least 12 credits every semester Graduate students are ordinarily required to complete 9 credits in order to be considered full-time. 4. Make normal, full-time progress toward program completion and complete within specified time periods (start and end date on I-20 or DS-2019). Extensions other than for medical or other unavoidable academic reasons are not permitted. 5. Obtain ISSS approval BEFORE a reduced course load registration is finalized. Retroactive approval of part-time enrollment once registration has ended is NOT possible. 6. Do not accept off-campus employment without written authorization from the ISSS or USCIS (Immigration authorities). Full-time students in F-1 or J-1 status work no more than 20 hours per week during the academic year and 40 hours during vacation periods and school breaks. 7. question: I work part time in the dining hall and my new landlord wants proof of my job and how much I make. Who in dining can write that?

body.answer:
Money stress is really common, and you don't have to sort it out alone.

People Operations and Employee Resources Department is the only department authorized to respond to employment verification inquiries. Verification confirms dates of employment, salary, and position(s) held; a written authorization and release signed by you is required. Verifications are usually provided within 48 hours of receipt. [21]

**People Operations and Employee Resources Department**: Phone: (201) 684-7506. Email: poer@ramapo.edu. Location: D-wing. [31]

These offices can help:
- **Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [32]
- **Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [32]

Sources: [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/poerd/employee-handbook/) [31](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [32](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: My employer reimburses tuition but they need an official paper showing I finished my summer course with a grade. Where do I get that?

body.answer:
To provide official proof showing your summer course grade, request an official paper copy of your transcript. Complete the Official Transcript Request Form and send it to transcript@ramapo.edu. There is no charge for an official paper copy. Processing takes 3–5 business days, with additional time possible during peak periods such as the start/end of a semester and during graduation. It cannot be emailed or faxed; it can be mailed to your employer or picked up in person with photo ID. [30]

You can also view your grades online through the Experience Webapp: select “FINAL GRADES” under the Student Records Menu, then select “Term” to view grades. [7]

**Admissions**: Phone: (201) 684-7300. Email: admissions@ramapo.edu. Location: McBride House. [35]

Sources: [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/faq/) [30](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/dual-enrollment/) [35](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: is there scholarship money for grad students going abroad? i want to apply before the deadline if there is

body.answer:
Yes. The Fulbright U.S. Student Program supports graduate study and research in over 140 countries. It is open to graduating seniors or graduate students in the U.S.; grants include book allowances, tuition, transportation, and a moderate dependence allowance. See [http://www.fulbrightonline.org/](http://www.fulbrightonline.org/) [19]

Other options listed include the Critical Language Scholarship, an intensive overseas language and cultural immersion program for American students enrolled at U.S. colleges and universities, and Boren Awards, Gilman Scholarship, and Marshall Scholarships. [20][21]

Ramapo's general scholarship deadline for the 26/27 academic year was 9/23/26; it has passed. [18] Completing the General Application at [http://ramapo.academicworks.com/](http://ramapo.academicworks.com/) is the first step to qualify for scholarships. Scholarship opportunities can change, so check the website, social media and Daily Digest often for updates and new opportunities. [18] For study-abroad scholarships, the Roukema Center for International Education lists resources including the Boren Scholarship and Critical Languages Scholarship. [1][2]

- **Transportation Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7432. Email: shuttle@ramapo.edu. [31]
- **Media Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7777. Email: mediahelpdesk@ramapo.edu. Office: H-205. [31]

question: I can't find a library book I borrowed and finals are here. What happens if I lost it, do I just pay for it?

body.answer:
Sorry to hear that!

For a regular library item, if it is not returned 28 days after the due date, a $75.00 fine ($50 replacement fee and $25 processing fee) is charged. The bill is added to your Office of Student Accounts account. Borrowing privileges are suspended for outstanding charges of $75 or more; transcripts and diplomas may also be held until charges are resolved. [1]

If you cannot find the book, ask Circulation staff for assistance and complete the missing-book form available at the Circulation Desk. Staff will search for it and notify you of the outcome. [3]

Contact the Library. Questions about book charges can be directed to Lili Pasaporte at lpasapor@ramapo.edu or Madel Tisi at mtisi@ramapo.edu. [1]

- **Library**: Phone: (201) 684-7575. Email: circ@ramapo.edu. Location: Peter P. Mercer Learning Commons. [24]
- **Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [24]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/library/circulation/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/library/circulation/) [24](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

Money stress is really common, and you don't have to sort it out alone.

Laboratory work is subject to normal deductibles and copays, even when drawn at Ramapo College Health Services. The 100% coverage applies to covered services such as routine primary care and preventive services; it does not make all medical care free. [1]
Contact Health Services to ask about the lab work and bill. [1]

**Health Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7536. Location: Near the campus South Gate entrance at the corner of Route 202 and Hornbeam Road. [33]

These offices can help:
- **Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [34]
- **Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [34]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/student-health-insurance/) [33](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [34](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

At check-in, residents receive a Room Inventory via their Ramapo college email. The Room Inventory contains information about the condition of the campus residence to which the student is assigned. There is an opportunity to dispute what is contained on the Room Inventory, which will be communicated upon check-in. After this time, it is assumed to be an accurate assessment of the condition of the residence and its contents. Residents are billed for damages, as they become known, often as a result of a room inspection. Damages are added to the student’s account. It is the student’s responsibility to see that damage bills are paid. (An outstanding balance on an account may result in a student’s inability to gain certain College services, to register, to obtain an official transcript, etc.). Malicious or repeated major damages may also result in disciplinary action in addition to charges for repair or replacement. After residents check-out of the residence halls at the end of the term, the Residence Life Staff will make a final inspection of the residence and compare the facility’s condition to the original inventories. Facilities staff makes the determination of the cost to repair any damage/loss. Depending on the situation, outside contractors may be used or College staff (often on overtime) may be assigned to repair damage/loss. Damage charges are assessed as a result of depreciating the value of the item that belongs to the college; not necessarily to be able to replace something or repair it to its original value. If more than one student occupies a space in which damage/loss occurs, the students will be held equally liable, unless one or more takes responsibility for the damage/loss. question: I'm in EOF and signed up to be a peer mentor for the summer program but I just got a job offer. Can I do only part of it or do I have to drop out

body.answer:
I can't choose for you, but I can share what the college publishes.

Ramapo describes the EOF Summer Studies Institute as a required, five-week program for incoming first-year EOF scholars; it says the program requires living on campus for its duration. [6] The FAQ also says incoming first-year students admitted through EOF are required to participate in the mandatory 5-week program; incoming EOF transfers are not required to participate. [10] I don’t find a published option to attend only part of it or guidance that you must drop out. The page does say students are required to return to campus Sunday evenings. [2]

The EOF Program says students can get one-on-one academic and personal advisement from an EOF Advisor, and EOF staff provide advising and ongoing support. [6][7] For help deciding, current students should contact their EOF Advisor or make an appointment in Connect; general questions can go to the EOF Program. [8]

**Educational Opportunity Fund (EOF) Program**: Phone: (201) 684-7541. Email: EOFdesk@ramapo.edu. Office: D-101. [24]

Sources: [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/eof-program/freshman/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/eof-program/freshman/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/eof-program/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/eof-program/) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/educational-opportunity-fund/faqs/) [24](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

answer:
I can't choose for you, but I can share what the college publishes.

Ramapo describes the EOF Summer Studies Institute as a required, five-week program for incoming first-year EOF scholars; it says the program requires living on campus for its duration. [6] The FAQ also says incoming first-year students admitted through EOF are required to participate in the mandatory 5-week program; incoming EOF transfers are not required to participate. [10] I don’t find a published option to attend only part of it or guidance that you must drop out. The page does say students are required to return to campus Sunday evenings. [2]

The EOF Program says students can get one-on-one academic and personal advisement from an EOF Advisor, and EOF staff provide advising and ongoing support. [6][7] For help deciding, current students should contact their EOF Advisor or make an appointment in Connect; general questions can go to the EOF Program. [8]

**Educational Opportunity Fund (EOF) Program**: Phone: (201) 684-7541. Email: EOFdesk@ramapo.edu. Office: D-101. [24]

Sources: [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/eof-program/freshman/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/eof-program/freshman/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/eof-program/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/eof-program/) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/educational-opportunity-fund/faqs/) [24](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: my bill says i owe for a meal plan but im a commuter and never picked one. the bill is due friday

body.answer:
Sorry to hear that!

Commuter students are not required to have a dining plan. If you did not choose one, email mealplan@ramapo.edu from your Ramapo email account with your full name and R number, and explain that you were charged for a plan you did not select. [16][19]
Your bill’s published payment deadline is December 16, 2026—not Friday, November 20. [5] Student Accounts says bills must be paid by the published deadlines. [7] Contact Student Accounts about the charge and deadline.

- **Dining Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7773. Location: Student Center, 1st Floor. [35]
- **Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [35]

question: my friend from home wants to visit and stay over in my room this weekend. do i have to register her somewhere

body.answer:
Yes. If she is 18 or older and not assigned to an on-campus room, she must complete the Guest Registration process if visiting after 10:00 PM; she must have valid ID and access to the approved registration email. [3] Each registered guest may stay no more than three nights within a seven-day period, and a night begins and ends at 10:00 PM. You may host up to two guests at a time, and she must stay with you. [2]

Overnight guests are not permitted on campus after Monday, December 14, 2026. [6]

For the registration process, see the Guest Procedures page: [https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [3]

**Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [34]

Sources: [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/fallcheckoutandwinter/) [34](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: is there a way to do bachelors and masters together in 5 years? i'd want to sign up early if thats a thing

body.answer:
Yes. Ramapo offers a 4+1 option to earn a bachelor’s and master’s degree in five years. For enrollment information and guidelines, contact the graduate program director. The Registrar’s page has the 4+1 Declaration Form: [https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/wp-content/uploads/sites/7/2026/04/41-Declaration-Form-FILLABLE.pdf](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/wp-content/uploads/sites/7/2026/04/41-Declaration-Form-FILLABLE.pdf) [1]

Listed programs include MS in Accounting, MA in Elementary/Special Education, Flex MBA, MSW, and Master of Public Policy. The MSW listing links to a 2021–2022 catalog, so I don’t have verified current information about that program. [9]

For details about signing up early, contact the graduate program director for the program you’re interested in. [1]

**Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [32]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/forms-transcripts/) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/admitted-students/academics/) [32](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: Everyone keeps talking about Handshake but I don't know what it is. Do I need it to find a job on campus?

body.answer:
Handshake is Ramapo’s job board and online career-management system. Students can use it to apply for jobs and internships, register for career fairs and events, and schedule Career Center appointments. [3][9]

Yes. All available on-campus positions are posted on Handshake, and you must register to view open positions. Search using the keyword “RCNJ,” follow each posting’s application instructions, and contact the supervisor listed. [24]

answer:
Handshake is Ramapo’s job board and online career-management system. Students can use it to apply for jobs and internships, register for career fairs and events, and schedule Career Center appointments. [3][9]

Yes. All available on-campus positions are posted on Handshake, and you must register to view open positions. Search using the keyword “RCNJ,” follow each posting’s application instructions, and contact the supervisor listed. [24]

To get started, go to [ramapo.joinhandshake.com](http://ramapo.joinhandshake.com/) and log on with single-service sign-on. [2]

**Cahill Career Development Center**: Phone: Main Office (201) 684-7444; ASB Office (201) 684-7675. Email: careercenter@ramapo.edu. Main Office: C-209; ASB Office: ASB-513. [30]

question: how do i get assigned an advisor? im undeclared and nobody ever contacted me

body.answer:
Sorry to hear that!

As an undeclared student, you’re assigned a professional advisor in the Center for Student Success through the Ramapo Exploration Program (REP). [7] Check your network in Connect for your assigned advisor. [10] Your assigned advisor is also shown at the bottom of your Degree Evaluation. [6]

If no advisor is listed, contact the Center for Student Success for advisement.

**Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [24]

Sources: [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/faq/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/myadvisor/) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/myadvisor/advisement-by-year/) [24](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: I'm signed up for 2 classes in my masters program for spring but I want to go down to 1 because of work. Is that allowed? I'm afraid of losing my aid

body.answer:
Money stress is really common, and you don't have to sort it out alone.

Whether one class is allowed depends on its credits and your specific aid; the information here doesn’t verify the enrollment requirements for your master’s program. Federal aid requires at least 6 credits in a semester. If dropping a class takes you below full-time, your aid may be adjusted; state aid may be canceled, and institutional grants or scholarships could be reduced or taken away. [1] NJ State aid such as TAG and EOF requires full-time enrollment when the aid is fully disbursed. [2]

Before changing your enrollment, discuss the impact on your aid with Financial Aid. [2][3] Check with your graduate program about whether one class meets its enrollment requirements; I don’t have verified information about that. Contact the Center for Student Success (Academic Advising).

- **Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [35]
- **Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [35]

This office can help:
**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [36]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/academic-merit-scholarships-terms-conditions/) [35](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [36](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: how do i give back my locker at the gym? im not going to use it next semester

body.answer:
If you mean the Student Center lockers, return the key at the end of the semester. [1] The page doesn’t specify a separate process for giving up the locker before next semester. Contact the Center for Student Involvement for guidance.

**Center for Student Involvement**: Phone: (201) 684-7593. Email: csi@ramapo.edu. Office: SC-202. [31]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/csi/) [31](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: i got charged for printing like 200 pages i never printed. i think someone is using my account. how do i fix it

body.answer:
Money stress is really common, and you don't have to sort it out alone.

Check your printing usage at [http://print.ramapo.edu](http://print.ramapo.edu). [1] Each student receives 200 pages per academic year at no charge; the allowance resets at the beginning of each academic year (each fall semester), and unused allowance will not roll over. [2] For a charge you don’t recognize or suspected account use, contact the IT Help Desk. I don’t have verified information about how to dispute or reverse a printing charge.

**IT Help Desk**: Phone: (201) 684-7777. Email: helpdesk@ramapo.edu. Location: 4th floor of the Learning Commons. [35]

These offices can help:
- **Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [36]
- **Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [36]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/its/mobile-printing/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/its/mobile-printing/) [35](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [36](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

answer:
Money stress is really common, and you don't have to sort it out alone.

Check your printing usage at [http://print.ramapo.edu](http://print.ramapo.edu). [1] Each student receives 200 pages per academic year at no charge; the allowance resets at the beginning of each academic year (each fall semester), and unused allowance will not roll over. [2] For a charge you don’t recognize or suspected account use, contact the IT Help Desk. I don’t have verified information about how to dispute or reverse a printing charge.

question: I lost my I-20 and I think my passport was in the same folder. What do I do first?

body.answer:
Sorry to hear that!

First, contact the Roukema Center for International Education about your lost I-20 and passport; the college advises speaking with an advisor there about questions related to your student status [21]. Keep copies of your passport picture page and current I-20 with you when available [21].

**Roukema Center for International Education**: Phone: (201) 684-7533. Location: C-wing, Suite 213. [30]

Sources: [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/public-safety-frequently-asked-questions/) [30](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

body.answer:

question: My parking ticket was due last week and I forgot about it. Now there's a late fee. Can I still pay it online?

body.answer:
Sorry to hear that!

Yes. Pay online through the Payment Portal: [https://rcnjpublicsafety.omnigo.one/CESIReportExec/OCP/Main.aspx](https://rcnjpublicsafety.omnigo.one/CESIReportExec/OCP/Main.aspx). Enter your Citation # and Fine Amount, search for the citation, select it, follow the required fields, and select a payment method. Once processed, your citation will be emailed to you as paid. [4]

Citations not paid or appealed within 20 days are subject to a $5 late fee; a second $5 late fee may be assessed after 28 days. [1] If you need to pay through Student Accounts during regular business hours, first stop at the Parking and ID Office, Rm. C101, or contact parking services at parking@ramapo.edu to ensure the fine has been transferred to your student account. [1]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [31]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/vehicle-citation-information/) [31](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: I am new international student starting in January. When should I arrive and who do I tell when I land?

body.answer:
For a Spring 2027 start, plan to arrive on or before the report date on your I-20 or DS-2019; do not arrive more than 30 days before that date. You must report to the Roukema Center for International Education no later than 15 days after your report date to complete mandatory check-in. [2][5]

Tell the Office of International Students and Scholars as early as possible your airline, flight number(s), departure and arrival times, and departure and arrival airports. You can email iosawami@ramapo.edu. [4]

If you’ll live on campus, Spring 2027 check-in is Monday, January 18, 2027, between 10:00am and 1:00pm. The College cannot accommodate check-in before that date. If you can’t arrive during the designated time, email your hall/area office staff with your anticipated arrival date. [25]

**Roukema Center for International Education**: Phone: (201) 684-7533. Location: C-wing, Suite 213. [28]

Sources: [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/inter-students/orientation/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/inter-students/transfer/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/inter-students/orientation/) [25](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/new-student-guide/) [28](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

answer:
For a Spring 2027 start, plan to arrive on or before the report date on your I-20 or DS-2019; do not arrive more than 30 days before that date. You must report to the Roukema Center for International Education no later than 15 days after your report date to complete mandatory check-in. [2][5]

Tell the Office of International Students and Scholars as early as possible your airline, flight number(s), departure and arrival times, and departure and arrival airports. You can email iosawami@ramapo.edu. [4]

If you’ll live on campus, Spring 2027 check-in is Monday, January 18, 2027, between 10:00am and 1:00pm. The College cannot accommodate check-in before that date. If you can’t arrive during the designated time, email your hall/area office staff with your anticipated arrival date. [25]

**Roukema Center for International Education**: Phone: (201) 684-7533. Location: C-wing, Suite 213. [28]

question: I see a counselor on campus but I'm home in another state for break. Can we still meet on video or is that not allowed?

body.answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [31]:
- Monday, September 7, 2026: Labor Day (College Closed - No Classes) (already passed)
- Wednesday, November 25, 2026: Thanksgiving Break (No Classes) (through November 29)
- Tuesday, December 8, 2026: Reading Day (No Classes)

Counseling appointments are conducted in person or via telehealth using a secure platform for audio/video communication [3]. The college does not say whether you can attend telehealth from another state, so I don’t have verified information about that. Contact the Counseling Center to confirm. For teletherapy through Uwill, register/login at [https://app.uwill.com/](https://app.uwill.com/) and choose a therapist and a time that fits your schedule [5].

**Counseling Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7522. Office: D-216. [32]

Sources: [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/faq/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/uwill/) [31](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/) [32](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: how do i get into the library databases from home? it keeps asking me to log in and my login doesnt work

body.answer:
Sorry to hear that!

Use the library’s [Databases A–Z](https://libguides.ramapo.edu/az/databases) page to open databases; off campus, links without the library’s proxy prefix won’t authenticate properly. Sign in with your Ramapo email username and Ramapo email password. Your username should not include “@ramapo.edu”; make sure the spelling is correct and Caps Lock is off. You must be a current Ramapo student, faculty member, or staff member, and your browser must accept cookies. [1][2][4]

If it still fails, try logging out of any VPN, clearing your browser history/cache/cookies, another browser or device, or a different internet connection. [4] See the [off-campus troubleshooting guide](https://www.ramapo.edu/library/off-campus-access-troubleshooting/). If you need technical help, contact the IT Help Desk.

- **Library**: Phone: (201) 684-7575. Email: circ@ramapo.edu. Location: Peter P. Mercer Learning Commons. [23]
- **IT Help Desk**: Phone: (201) 684-7777. Email: helpdesk@ramapo.edu. Location: 4th floor of the Learning Commons. [23]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/library/off-campus-access-instructions/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/library/off-campus-access-troubleshooting/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/library/off-campus-access-troubleshooting/) [23](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: advisor said my stats class from my last school only counts as an elective not for my major. i dont get it, its the same class. can i ask for someone to look at it again

body.answer:
Yes. If academic approval for a non-general education course equivalency has not yet been established, it counts as elective credit, but not toward a particular degree program. To have the course evaluated for your major, contact the Convener of the appropriate program to review the course and its potential for transfer credit. If approved, the Convener sends the approval to the Office of Admissions, which designates a person to update the appropriate systems. [2]

I don't have verified information about who your program’s Convener is. Contact the Office of the Provost for help identifying them.

- **Admissions**: Phone: (201) 684-7300. Email: admissions@ramapo.edu. Location: McBride House. [33]
- **Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [33]

question: I graduate in May and just found out I should have applied for OPT already?? Is it too late and what do I do

body.answer:
Sorry to hear that!

I don’t have verified information about whether it’s too late for a May graduate or the OPT application deadline. Contact the Roukema Center for International Education as soon as possible. To be eligible for OPT, you must be in valid F-1 immigration status and have completed at least one academic year (two semesters) of full-time study. [1]

The Center lists an OPT Form (PDF): [https://www.ramapo.edu/inter-students/wp-content/uploads/sites/232/2013/11/opt-form.pdf](https://www.ramapo.edu/inter-students/wp-content/uploads/sites/232/2013/11/opt-form.pdf) [3]

**Roukema Center for International Education**: Phone: (201) 684-7533. Location: C-wing, Suite 213. [34]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/inter-students/current/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/inter-students/forms/) [34](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: I stay on campus over winter break and my meal swipes don't work at the dining hall. How do I get food?

body.answer:
I'm sorry you're dealing with that. You're not alone, and you can ask for help.

You can apply to the Swipe Out Hunger Program for 5 meals at the Birch Tree Inn. It is for currently enrolled students experiencing food insecurity; availability is limited. Students with Ultimate or Maroon 14 meal plans are not eligible. New applicants and students without a meal plan get priority; repeat applicants may be considered case by case. Apply here: [https://cglink.me/2fF/s60806](https://cglink.me/2fF/s60806). Questions: wecare@ramapo.edu. [10]

You can also take free ready-to-eat items from the campus satellite pantries. For more items or a larger selection, go to the food pantry in ASB 130. [12]

**Civic and Community Engagement Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7586. Email: ccec@ramapo.edu. Office: SC-213. [32]

Sources: [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/ccec/we-care-program/food-insecurity-resources/) [12](https://www.ramapo.edu/ccec/we-care-program/food-insecurity-resources/) [32](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: I want to drop one class but then I would have only 9 credits. Can I drop it and add a different one this week?

body.answer:
You can adjust your schedule from your registration day through the last day of Add/Drop. After that, you can no longer add classes to your schedule. Check the Academic Calendar for this term’s deadline: [https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/) [8][1]

At 9 credits, you would be part-time; full-time is at least 12 credits. [29][20] Dropping below full-time may adjust financial aid. Federal aid requires at least 6 credits; state aid and institutional grants or scholarships could be reduced or canceled. [3]

Because the applicable deadline this week isn’t provided here, I don’t have verified information about whether you can make this change this week. Contact the Registrar to confirm the deadline and your options. [7][8]

- **Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [35]
- **Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [35]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/faq/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/registrationinfo/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/faq/) [20](https://www.ramapo.edu/orientation/faq-2/) [29](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/returning-student/) [35](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

During the first year of membership, members are required to participate in the contributory coverage to provide an additional 1-1/2 times the pro-rated annual salary coverage at a cost (payroll deduction) to the employee of 0.50 of 1% of his/her annual salary. question: lost my phone and now i cant get the login code for my school account. how do i get back in

body.answer:
Sorry to hear that!

Contact the IT Help Desk for help regaining access to your account. You can call 201-684-7777, email helpdesk@ramapo.edu, or visit in person on the 4th floor of the Learning Commons. [2]

**IT Help Desk**: Phone: (201) 684-7777. Email: helpdesk@ramapo.edu. Location: 4th floor of the Learning Commons. [33]

question: my aid for spring looks way lower than fall and i didnt change anything. how do i find out why and fix it

body.answer:
I can't see your personal records, like your grades, balance, schedule or financial aid status.

Check whether your enrollment changed: dropping below full-time can adjust aid. If you go from 12 credits to 6, your federal Pell will be reduced but you can keep federal loans; state aid may be canceled and institutional grants and scholarships could be reduced or taken away. Federal aid requires at least 6 credits. [1] NJ State aid (such as TAG and EOF) requires full-time enrollment when aid is fully disbursed. [2]

Compare your spring award with fall and review any changes to the information you provided on your FAFSA. Your Student Aid Index (SAI) is calculated from FAFSA information, but it is not your financial aid award. [3]

To find out what caused the difference and discuss a re-evaluation, email or call the Office of Financial Aid. You can also schedule an appointment by email or through the chat on the Financial Aid website. In-person appointments are Monday through Friday, 8:30am to 4:30pm; questions can also be handled by phone, Webex, or email. [7]

**Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [33]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/understanding-your-financial-aid-award/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/) [33](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: I applied to the honors program and got rejected but they said I can reapply? I don't understand what I'm supposed to do differently or when

body.answer:
I can't choose for you, but I can share what the college publishes. That's stressful, but one bad grade doesn't decide everything. Talking with your professor and an advisor soon can really help.

Since you were rejected, you may reapply at the end of your first semester at Ramapo. [1] The current-Ramapo-freshmen page says the application window is December 1 to January 8; you must have a 3.50 GPA from the fall semester. [7]

Email PDFs of these materials with the subject line “Honors Application”: [7]
1. An admission essay of 800 words or less, answering the prompt about a community you belong to and your place within it. [7]
2. One recommendation from a Ramapo faculty member. Ask them to send it to Director Erin Augis at eaugis@ramapo.edu; the letter should show personal knowledge of your intellectual independence and capacity for engaged learning. [7]
3. A previously completed essay or project from your first semester at Ramapo that demonstrates the qualities required for admission. Include a description of the assignment and class; attach it as a regular PDF, not an embedded link. [7]

The catalog says to send these materials to honors@ramapo.edu. [2] The current-students page says to email them to eaugis@ramapo.edu (its mail link points to honors@ramapo.edu). [7] I don’t have verified information resolving which address to use; contact the Ramapo Honors Program.

**Ramapo Honors Program**: Email: honors@ramapo.edu. [29]

This office can help:
**Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [30]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/quicklinks/academicpolicies#college-honors-program1) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/quicklinks/academicpolicies#college-honors-program1) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/honors/applications/current-ramapo-students/) [29](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [30](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

answer:
I can't choose for you, but I can share what the college publishes. That's stressful, but one bad grade doesn't decide everything. Talking with your professor and an advisor soon can really help.

Since you were rejected, you may reapply at the end of your first semester at Ramapo. [1] The current-Ramapo-freshmen page says the application window is December 1 to January 8; you must have a 3.50 GPA from the fall semester. [7]

Email PDFs of these materials with the subject line “Honors Application”: [7]
1. An admission essay of 800 words or less, answering the prompt about a community you belong to and your place within it. [7]
2. One recommendation from a Ramapo faculty member. Ask them to send it to Director Erin Augis at eaugis@ramapo.edu; the letter should show personal knowledge of your intellectual independence and capacity for engaged learning. [7]
3. A previously completed essay or project from your first semester at Ramapo that demonstrates the qualities required for admission. Include a description of the assignment and class; attach it as a regular PDF, not an embedded link. [7]

The catalog says to send these materials to honors@ramapo.edu. [2] The current-students page says to email them to eaugis@ramapo.edu (its mail link points to honors@ramapo.edu). [7] I don’t have verified information resolving which address to use; contact the Ramapo Honors Program.

**Ramapo Honors Program**: Email: honors@ramapo.edu. [29]

This office can help:
**Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [30]

question: I went to the testing center to take my final with extra time and they said they have no request from my professor. My exam is tomorrow. What can I do?

body.answer:
You can ask for support with that.

Contact your instructor immediately to make sure your exam accommodations are set up. [18] Faculty are responsible for providing alternative testing arrangements. [17] OSS exam reservations are normally due no later than five business days in advance, excluding weekends and holidays, and ten business days for final exams. [17] Since your exam is tomorrow, contact your OSS counselor or an Alternative Testing staff member right away for guidance. [20]

If you made an exam reservation, faculty should receive an email with exam details and an upload link; exam uploads are due by 12pm the day before the exam. [17] If faculty did not receive an email, they may assume you are taking the exam in class as usual. [21]

If you have not made an exam reservation, contact the Office of Specialized Services. [17]

**Office of Specialized Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7514. Email: oss@ramapo.edu. Location: C-Wing, Room 205. [27]

Sources: [17](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/what-faculty-need-to-know-about-students-with-disabilities/) [18](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/alternative-testing-for-students/) [20](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/alternative-testing-for-faculty/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/alternative-testing-for-faculty/faqs-about-testing-for-faculty/) [27](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: trying to sign up for a class for spring and it says prerequisite or test score error. i took the prereq as an AP class in high school. what do i do

body.answer:
Check your transcript/DegreeWorks audit to ensure you have the prerequisite. [1] Ramapo awards AP credit for scores of 4 or 5; submit the official score report to the Office of Admissions. [27] If you can prove you satisfied the prerequisite but still cannot register, contact the academic school that offers the course. The unit secretary may place an override on your record, allowing you to register. [15] You can also see the instructor to request an electronic override; the instructor enters overrides. You must still register online after it is entered. [18]

**Admissions**: Phone: (201) 684-7300. Email: admissions@ramapo.edu. Location: McBride House. [33]

I don’t have verified information about guest passes or whether your brother can use the gym, even if he pays. The Lodge Fitness Center is managed by Athletics [5]; contact Athletics to ask about guest access.

**Athletics**: Phone: (201) 684-7674. [32]

Sources: [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/college-park-apartments-cpa/) [32](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: I already have extra test time from the disability office but now I also need help with notes because I hurt my hand. How do I add that?

body.answer:
I'm sorry you're dealing with that, and I hope you feel better soon.

Contact the Office of Specialized Services to request the additional note-taking accommodation. Accommodations are determined on a case-by-case basis. [18] OSS lists notetakers or scribes as potential accommodations for health impairments. [16] All accommodation requests must be supported by documentation from a qualified professional, and students must complete an Affiliation Packet. Request the packet using the OSS Quick Response Form: [https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/oss-quick-response-form/](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/oss-quick-response-form/) or contact OSS by email at oss@ramapo.edu. Send the completed packet and supporting documentation electronically to oss@ramapo.edu. [21]

**Office of Specialized Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7514. Email: oss@ramapo.edu. Location: C-Wing, Room 205. [30]

This office can help:
**Health Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7536. Location: Near the campus South Gate entrance at the corner of Route 202 and Hornbeam Road. [31]

Sources: [16](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/disabilities-and-teaching-strategies-accommodations/) [18](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/disabilities-and-teaching-strategies-accommodations/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/documentation-requirements/) [30](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [31](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

Psychological disabilities may include, but are not limited to, anxiety disorders, depression, bipolar, schizophrenia, and obsessive-compulsive disorder. These conditions (and sometimes the medication used to treat the conditions) can lead to difficulties with attention and concentration, extreme worry, excessive fatigue, lack of sleep, excessive energy, and difficulties regulating emotions, among other symptoms and side-effects. Students’ symptoms and academic performance may vary from day to day. Since their condition is not necessarily obvious, it can be difficult for peers and faculty to understand why a student may be having difficulty functioning socially or academically. We are unable to share any clinical information with faculty about the nature of the disability unless the student has given us explicit written permission. Note: If a student discloses a psychological disability to you, please do not ask the student to share details of the disability if he or she does not wish to share information. It is the expectation of the College that students attend and arrive on time to all class meetings. If a student needs to miss class due to a psychological disability when their condition flairs, OSS will collaborate with the professor, the student, and their dean in advance to identify a clear policy on absences so as not to alter fundamental course requirements. Each instructor has the right to determine their own individual attendance policy. Students are responsible for accounting to their instructors any absence and should contact the faculty member following any absence to determine if and when work may be made up. OSS is happy to consult with students and faculty to determine what is appropriate in specific circumstances. These include, but are not limited to, arthritis, cancer, Irritable Bowel Syndrome, Multiple Sclerosis, asthma, AIDS, Crohn’s, and heart disease. Unless the condition is neurological in nature, health impairments are not likely to directly affect learning. However, the secondary effects of illness and the side effects of medications can have a significant impact on memory, attention, strength, endurance, and energy levels. It is the expectation of the College that students attend and arrive on time to all class meetings. If a student needs to miss class due to a medical disability when their condition flairs, OSS will collaborate with the professor and the student in advance to identify a clear policy on absences so as not to alter fundamental course requirements. Each instructor has the right to determine their own individual attendance policy. Students are responsible for accounting to their instructors any absence and should contact the faculty member following any absence to determine if and when work may be made up. OSS is happy to consult with students and faculty to determine what is appropriate in specific circumstances. Examples of ways impairment may affect a student’s ability to participate include: Missing class for unpredictable and prolonged time periods Health problems may also interfere with the physical skills needed to complete laboratory, computer, or writing assignments Individuals with arthritis, for example, may have difficulty writing due to pain or joint deformities, making it a challenge for them to meet the writing requirements for some classes Students with Multiple Sclerosis may not be able to manipulate small laboratory equipment or complete tasks that require precise measuring, graphing, or drawing Prolonged sitting may pose challenges for an individual with chronic pain or back problems Illness or injury may result in limitations in mobility which require the need to use a wheelchair or scooter for mobility Some students must avoid specific activities that trigger their conditions. For example, a student with asthma may need to avoid specific inhalants in a lab. Potential Accommodations / Teaching Strategies: Notetakers or scribes Audio-recording of classes Flexible attendance policy Short-term extensions on assignments when possible Extended testing time or alternative testing arrangements Assignments available in electronic format Electronic distribution of course materials Speech recognition computer input devices When health conditions result in mobility problems, accommodations for students with mobility impairments may be appropriate. This monthly benefit is offset by any other periodic benefit the member may be receiving, such as Workers’ Compensation, short-term disability, or Social Security. In addition, while the member is considered disabled, the member’s and the employer’s mandatory contributions are automatically credited to the member’s retirement account. Each employee must contribute a payroll tax with a maximum deduction in each calendar year. The wage base for premium deductions will vary each year with the State-wide average weekly wage of the preceding year. Each claimant is paid two-thirds (2/3) of his/her average weekly wage up to the maximum amount payable set for that calendar year. The weekly maximum benefit is payable for no more than 26 weeks and a claim cannot be filed until exhaustion of accumulated sick leave. If they can be reasonably accommodated without undue hardship to the Unit/College, the employee will be permitted to return to work for modified duty. Supervisors and returning employees must ensure only permitted activities are performed by the employee as prescribed by the treating physician. In the event that an employee is unable to resume the full duties of the position within 12 weeks, leave options under the Federal Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) will be reviewed, as well as eligibility for State temporary disability, Sick Leave Injury (SLI), or temporary workers’ compensation benefits. If the employee still remains disabled following exhaustion of leave entitlements (accrued time, FMLA and any contractual entitlements), the employee may be sent for a fitness-for- duty exam, at the College’s expense, to determine if the restrictions are permanent in nature. If a determination is made that the restrictions are permanent in nature, every attempt will be made to consider whether the employee can perform the duties of an available position on campus for which the employee qualifies with or without reasonable accommodation. If such a position is not available, and the employee is unable to perform the duties of the employee’s position, separation from the College will ensue. question: im the treasurer of our club and the form to request money for our event keeps giving an error. the event is in 2 weeks

body.answer:
Sorry to hear that!

For SGA co-sponsorship, fill out the co-sponsorship request form on Archway: [https://cglink.me/2fF/s60091](https://cglink.me/2fF/s60091) [1]. I don’t have verified information about what to do if the form errors or whether an event in two weeks meets the funding timeline; contact Student Government Association.

**Student Government Association**: Phone: (201) 684-7271. Email: sga@ramapo.edu. Office: SC-225. [34]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/sga/faq/) [34](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

The funds are to be deposited in the GL system 10001-1002 by the old fiduciary and reconciled using the reconciliation form. A new Petty Cash or Change Fund Custodian Form and Accounts Payable Voucher Form should be filled out by the new fiduciary and signed off by the Controller to establish the new change fund. Petty Cash Fund The petty cash fund custodian is a person designated by the Controller. This person should follow the Change Fund procedure with regard to establishing, reconciling and replenishing the petty cash fund. This person will assist the Controller with managing the change funds throughout the College. A petty cash fund is to be used to pay relatively small expenses that are appropriate, necessary and reasonable to conduct College business, such as: Freight and delivery charges; Office supplies; Research and lab supplies; Transportation to and from unexpected meetings and conferences; Similar miscellaneous items; or Incidental meeting expenses; incidental meals. The Petty Cash fund should not be used for: The purchase of postage stamps for resale; Personal loans or other personal purposes (i.e., no check cashing); Items of $25 or more which can be anticipated and requisitioned in accordance with the establishment of a checking account; Any travel expenses related to overnight travel (other than toll charges, mileage and parking); or Paying students or departmental workers. question: Is the health center open on Saturday during finals week?

body.answer:
Health Services doesn't publish hours for Saturday, November 21 (checked November 17, 2026). [2]

Health Services's page "Health Services" says: "Ramapo College has partnered with Valley Medical Group to manage our on-campus Health Services Center. This agreement ensures that students and employees have direct access to high-quality clinical care, virtual telehealth visits, and coordinated referrals to Valley specialists throughout northern New Jersey. View Valley Medical Group Health Services ([https://www.valleyhealth.com/ramapo-college-health-services](https://www.valleyhealth.com/ramapo-college-health-services))" [1]

Dean of Students's page "Official Announcement: Health Services at Ramapo College" says: "From: The Dean of Students <deanofstudents@ramapo.edu> Date: Tue, Jul 14, 2026 at 2:03 PM Subject: Official Announcement: Health Services at Ramapo College Dear Student: Ramapo College has partnered with Valley Medical Group (VMG) to deliver high-quality, comprehensive, and compassionate medical care to students and employees right on campus. Located at the South Entrance, VMG will be open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. in the Fall semester (summer hours are Monday through Thursday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.)." (more on its page) [3]

Office of Specialized Services's page "Health Services" says: "Health Services ([https://www.ramapo.edu/health/](https://www.ramapo.edu/health/)) All currently enrolled students are eligible to use Health Services free of charge. If you need assistance getting to Health Services for your appointment, please contact Campus Security at x6666. Appointments: Please call (201) 684-7536 (off campus) or X 7536 (on campus) to schedule your appointment. All patients are seen on an appointment basis. Emergencies are seen immediately. Due to the limited number of appointments available, patients are asked to call and cancel an appointment if you are unable to keep it." (more on its page) [4]

I don't have verified information about that part.

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/health/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-affairs/student-communications/official-announcement-health-services-at-ramapo-college-july-14-2026/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-affairs/student-communications/official-announcement-health-services-at-ramapo-college-july-14-2026/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/campus-resources/)

Office of Specialized Services's page "Health Services" says: "Health Services ([https://www.ramapo.edu/health/](https://www.ramapo.edu/health/)) All currently enrolled students are eligible to use Health Services free of charge. Appointments: Please call (201) 684-7536 (off campus) or X 7536 (on campus) to schedule your appointment. All patients are seen on an appointment basis. Emergencies are seen immediately. I don't have verified information about that part.

question: what laptop should i get for school, mac or windows?

body.answer: **General answer** (from general knowledge, not Ramapo's pages): Either can work well for school. Choose a Mac if you prefer macOS, already use Apple devices, or need strong battery life; choose Windows for more model and price options, gaming, or software that requires Windows. Check your program’s required software first, since some courses need a specific operating system.
