question: is it better to take 15 or 18 credits first semester

body.answer:
I can't choose for you, but I can share what the college publishes.

Ramapo publishes that tuition and tuition-related fees are a flat rate between 12 and 18 credits. Ramapo courses are four credits and most students take four courses per semester, averaging 16 credits. Taking 16 credits each semester for eight semesters allows students to meet the 128-credit graduation requirement. [1]

For your first semester, Ramapo says first-year students are placed into four courses based on their declared major; if undeclared, they are assigned general education courses. [9] The published guidance doesn’t say whether 15 or 18 credits is better specifically.

First-year students are assigned a professional advisor in the Center for Student Success; check Connect to find your assigned advisor. [14] Students meet an advisor during their In Person Advisement session; follow the steps in your Admissions portal for details. [5] Ramapo recommends seeing your designated advisor to discuss course selection. [9]

- **Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [34]
- **Admissions**: Phone: (201) 684-7300. Email: admissions@ramapo.edu. Location: McBride House. [34]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/orientation/faq-2/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/orientation/faq-2/) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/myadvisor/advisement-by-year/) [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/myadvisor/advisement-by-year/) [34](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

answer:
I can't choose for you, but I can share what the college publishes.

Ramapo publishes that tuition and tuition-related fees are a flat rate between 12 and 18 credits. Ramapo courses are four credits and most students take four courses per semester, averaging 16 credits. Taking 16 credits each semester for eight semesters allows students to meet the 128-credit graduation requirement. [1]

For your first semester, Ramapo says first-year students are placed into four courses based on their declared major; if undeclared, they are assigned general education courses. [9] The published guidance doesn’t say whether 15 or 18 credits is better specifically.

First-year students are assigned a professional advisor in the Center for Student Success; check Connect to find your assigned advisor. [14] Students meet an advisor during their In Person Advisement session; follow the steps in your Admissions portal for details. [5] Ramapo recommends seeing your designated advisor to discuss course selection. [9]

- **Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [34]
- **Admissions**: Phone: (201) 684-7300. Email: admissions@ramapo.edu. Location: McBride House. [34]

Uwill’s counselors are: Fully licensed; Completed mandatory diversity & cultural competency training; Average 12 years of clinical experience; 50 states and international coverage; 11 languages spoken; 40% identify as BIPOC; 25% identify as LGBTQIA+. (http://app.uwill.com/) More information about Uwill and Counseling Services can be found on the Counseling Services website (https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/). Counseling Services offers comprehensive mental health services for students including access to in-person (and virtual) therapists, 24/7 emergency crisis intervention services, access to a psychiatrist, and drop-in hours. Drop-in hours are brief, confidential meetings with one of our counselors to discuss a specific concern. For drop-in hours, no appointment is necessary and students are seen on a first-come, first-served basis Monday-Thursday (for summer), 1:00pm to 3:00pm in D-216 (or virtual) by calling 201-684-7522. question: what should i get my roommate for christmas, she likes plants

body.answer: **General answer** (from general knowledge, not Ramapo's pages): A small, easy-care plant in a cute pot is a safe bet. Other thoughtful ideas: propagation jars, plant-themed art, a watering can, or a gift card to a local plant shop. If she has lots of plants already, choose something practical like a moisture meter or pruning shears.

question: Is there a club for international students, or for Indian students?

body.answer:
Yes. The International Student Organization (ISO) welcomes students of all nationalities and plans activities for members and the Ramapo community. Its events include international dinner nights, films, lectures, off-campus trips, International Student Week, and the International Food Festival. Email iso@ramapo.edu. [https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/organization/international-student-organization-iso/](https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/organization/international-student-organization-iso/) [21]

For Indian or South Asian students, the South Asian Club brings South Asians together and raises awareness of South Asian culture; its events highlight South Asian music, art, and traditions. Anyone interested in experiencing South Asian culture is welcome. Email southasians@ramapo.edu. [https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/organization/south-asians-ramapo/](https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/organization/south-asians-ramapo/) [24][3]

Naach is an inclusive dance club teaching South Asian dances, including Bollywood, Nepali Folk Dance, and South Asian classical styles. Email naach@ramapo.edu. [https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/organization/naach/](https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/organization/naach/) [27]

**Center for Student Involvement**: Phone: (201) 684-7593. Email: csi@ramapo.edu. Office: SC-202. [59]

question: how many credits do i still need for my major

body.answer:
I can't see your personal records, like your grades, balance, schedule or financial aid status.

I can’t tell how many credits you personally still need from the information provided. Your major’s requirements vary; review your Degree Evaluation and meet with your adviser to confirm where you stand. [1][3]

To view the evaluation outlining class requirements for your major: [14]
1. Visit [https://web.ramapo.edu/](https://web.ramapo.edu/) and click on Web for Students.
2. Click on Web Registration, enter the Secure Area, and type in your Ramapo login and password.
3. Click on Student and Financial Aid, then Student Records, then Degree Evaluation.
4. Select the current term and click enter. Click Generate New Evaluation, click the circle next to your major, and click Generate Request.
5. Select detail requirements and click Submit.

The Degree Audit tool is also available at [https://web.ramapo.edu/degree-audit-tools/](https://web.ramapo.edu/degree-audit-tools/). [6]

**Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [36]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/faq/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/faq/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/home/comprehensive-academic-plan/resources/) [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/faq/) [36](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

I can’t tell how many credits you personally still need from the information provided. Your major’s requirements vary; review your Degree Evaluation and meet with your adviser to confirm where you stand. [1][3]

To view the evaluation outlining class requirements for your major: [14]
1. Visit [https://web.ramapo.edu/](https://web.ramapo.edu/) and click on Web for Students.
2. Click on Web Registration, enter the Secure Area, and type in your Ramapo login and password.
3. Click on Student and Financial Aid, then Student Records, then Degree Evaluation.
4. Select the current term and click enter. Click Generate New Evaluation, click the circle next to your major, and click Generate Request.
5. Select detail requirements and click Submit.

The Degree Audit tool is also available at [https://web.ramapo.edu/degree-audit-tools/](https://web.ramapo.edu/degree-audit-tools/). [6]

**Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [36]

question: is it worth getting a masters right after graduating or should i work first

body.answer:
**General answer** (from general knowledge, not Ramapo's pages): It depends on your field, finances, and whether you already know what you want to specialize in. Go straight into a master’s if it’s required for your career or you have a clear goal; working first can help you test your interests, build experience, and avoid paying for a degree you may not need. Compare job requirements, program costs, funding, and likely earnings before deciding.

Ramapo’s published information does not say whether it is better to start a master’s right after graduating or work first. It says graduates may go on to graduate school or the workplace, and that they enter the next level familiar with that field’s day-to-day realities. [3]

For help weighing career plans, contact the Cahill Career Development Center. Its career advisors help with career-related guidance, and students can schedule appointments through Handshake. [21] The Center for Student Success specializes in helping students choose majors, but the published advice is about choosing a major, not deciding when to pursue graduate school. [10]

- **Cahill Career Development Center**: Phone: Main Office (201) 684-7444; ASB Office (201) 684-7675. Email: careercenter@ramapo.edu. Main Office: C-209; ASB Office: ASB-513. [34]
- **Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [34]

Sources: [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/admitted-students/outcomes/) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/major/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/careercenter/four-year-plan/) [34](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

answer:
**General answer** (from general knowledge, not Ramapo's pages): It depends on your field, finances, and whether you already know what you want to specialize in. Go straight into a master’s if it’s required for your career or you have a clear goal; working first can help you test your interests, build experience, and avoid paying for a degree you may not need. Compare job requirements, program costs, funding, and likely earnings before deciding.

Ramapo’s published information does not say whether it is better to start a master’s right after graduating or work first. It says graduates may go on to graduate school or the workplace, and that they enter the next level familiar with that field’s day-to-day realities. [3]

For help weighing career plans, contact the Cahill Career Development Center. Its career advisors help with career-related guidance, and students can schedule appointments through Handshake. [21] The Center for Student Success specializes in helping students choose majors, but the published advice is about choosing a major, not deciding when to pursue graduate school. [10]

- **Cahill Career Development Center**: Phone: Main Office (201) 684-7444; ASB Office (201) 684-7675. Email: careercenter@ramapo.edu. Main Office: C-209; ASB Office: ASB-513. [34]
- **Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [34]

Sources: [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/admitted-students/outcomes/) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/major/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/careercenter/four-year-plan/) [34](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: Is there an application fee for grad school here?

body.answer:
Yes. Graduate applicants must submit the application with a non-refundable $65 application fee or fee waiver. [1]

**Graduate Admissions**: Phone: (201) 684-7270. Email: graduate@ramapo.edu. Location: McBride House. [31]

question: Which clubs do you recommend to meet American students?

body.answer:
**General answer** (from general knowledge, not Ramapo's pages): Try clubs centered on shared interests—intramural sports, outdoor activities, volunteering, performing arts, or games—since those make it easy to talk and work together. Choose a couple that meet regularly and welcome newcomers; casual conversation often grows naturally from doing things side by side.

Ramapo does not specifically recommend clubs for meeting American students. It says all clubs are open to all students, welcomes new members, and that joining can help students make interesting friends. Its club page lists more than 80 groups, and the directory includes cultural, academic, religious, recreational, entertainment, political, social and special-interest clubs. [6]

To meet people through shared interests, consider the American Marketing Association, open to all majors, or Black American Music Club, which offers a space to explore music rooted in Black American culture. [8][11] The directory also lists American Medical Womens Association, Filipino American Student Association and American Cancer Society On Campus. [1][4][5]

The Center for Student Involvement can help you explore clubs and decide what fits; Ramapo says students who do not find their interests represented should inquire there about starting a new club. [6]

**Center for Student Involvement**: Phone: (201) 684-7593. Email: csi@ramapo.edu. Office: SC-202. [62]

Sources: [1](https://archway.ramapo.edu/AMWAC/) [4](https://archway.ramapo.edu/FASA/) [5](https://archway.ramapo.edu/ACS/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/organization/american-marketing-association-ama/) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/organization/black-american-music-club-bam/) [62](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

answer:
**General answer** (from general knowledge, not Ramapo's pages): Try clubs centered on shared interests—intramural sports, outdoor activities, volunteering, performing arts, or games—since those make it easy to talk and work together. Choose a couple that meet regularly and welcome newcomers; casual conversation often grows naturally from doing things side by side.

Ramapo does not specifically recommend clubs for meeting American students. It says all clubs are open to all students, welcomes new members, and that joining can help students make interesting friends. Its club page lists more than 80 groups, and the directory includes cultural, academic, religious, recreational, entertainment, political, social and special-interest clubs. [6]

To meet people through shared interests, consider the American Marketing Association, open to all majors, or Black American Music Club, which offers a space to explore music rooted in Black American culture. [8][11] The directory also lists American Medical Womens Association, Filipino American Student Association and American Cancer Society On Campus. [1][4][5]

The Center for Student Involvement can help you explore clubs and decide what fits; Ramapo says students who do not find their interests represented should inquire there about starting a new club. [6]

**Center for Student Involvement**: Phone: (201) 684-7593. Email: csi@ramapo.edu. Office: SC-202. [62]

question: which is better here, the MBA or the masters in accounting

body.answer:
I can't choose for you, but I can share what the college publishes.

Ramapo describes the M.S. in Accounting (MSAC) as an AACSB-accredited, 30-credit program preparing students for CPA and accounting/control-function careers. It offers spring, summer, and fall starts. [7] Its catalog says the program prepares students for CPA and accounting/management advisory roles; in combination with an undergraduate degree, students would attain the 150 credits required to sit for the CPA examination. [1]

Ramapo describes the MBA as an AACSB-accredited, 42-credit, 20-month cohort program focused on preparing graduates for management and senior-level business careers, with fall starts only. [8] The catalog describes it as preparing leaders for commercial enterprises and nonprofits, with a 30-credit Advanced Standing Program and a 42-credit program. The 42-credit program includes six foundational courses (2 credits each) plus 30 credits of core and elective courses; students in Advanced Standing do not need the foundational courses. [2]

The pages describe different goals, but don’t say which is better for you. For help deciding, the Graduate Admissions Counselor can discuss questions about earning a master’s degree and help you choose a career path. Email graduate@ramapo.edu to schedule an appointment. [14]

**Graduate Admissions**: Phone: (201) 684-7270. Email: graduate@ramapo.edu. Location: McBride House. [16]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SB-MS-MSAC) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SB-MBA-MBAD) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/graduate/home/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/graduate/home/) [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/learn/graduate/) [16](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

answer:
I can't choose for you, but I can share what the college publishes.

Ramapo describes the M.S. in Accounting (MSAC) as an AACSB-accredited, 30-credit program preparing students for CPA and accounting/control-function careers. It offers spring, summer, and fall starts. [7] Its catalog says the program prepares students for CPA and accounting/management advisory roles; in combination with an undergraduate degree, students would attain the 150 credits required to sit for the CPA examination. [1]

Ramapo describes the MBA as an AACSB-accredited, 42-credit, 20-month cohort program focused on preparing graduates for management and senior-level business careers, with fall starts only. [8] The catalog describes it as preparing leaders for commercial enterprises and nonprofits, with a 30-credit Advanced Standing Program and a 42-credit program. The 42-credit program includes six foundational courses (2 credits each) plus 30 credits of core and elective courses; students in Advanced Standing do not need the foundational courses. [2]

The pages describe different goals, but don’t say which is better for you. For help deciding, the Graduate Admissions Counselor can discuss questions about earning a master’s degree and help you choose a career path. Email graduate@ramapo.edu to schedule an appointment. [14]

**Graduate Admissions**: Phone: (201) 684-7270. Email: graduate@ramapo.edu. Location: McBride House. [16]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SB-MS-MSAC) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SB-MBA-MBAD) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/graduate/home/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/graduate/home/) [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/learn/graduate/) [16](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

Direct deposit is also known as Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT). It is the transfer of funds from Ramapo College to an individual student’s checking or savings account at a participating bank, savings and loan association or credit union. Direct deposit delivers your money quickly and safely. The difference is a check isn’t printed or mailed. Are there any costs for my participating in Direct Deposit? No, the program is offered as a service to our students. I’m interested in Direct Deposit, but I do not know if it is for me? If you have an account, visit your bank or credit union. They can answer your questions about Direct Deposit. If you do not have an account, consider opening one. Many banks offer a variety of accounts, some with little or no fees. Where do I sign up for Direct Deposit? Click here for instructions (https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit/). The Payment Profile asks for my checking or saving account number and my bank’s transit routing number. How do I find that information? Checking and savings account numbers are normally noted at the bottom of checks and deposit slips as well as the nine digit bank transit routing number. If you need assistance, come to the Office of Student Accounts, first floor, D-Wing. When I sign up for Direct Deposit, how long does it take before my money is available in my account? When you sign up for Direct Deposit, you can expect your refund to be deposited into your account within one to two weeks of the application being submitted. This pertains only to students that are eligible for a refund because of either overpayment by a loan or financial aid or for students that drop classes within the appropriate add/drop dates. When can I use my money? Your money is available for use as soon as it is deposited into your account. You can write checks, withdraw money and transfer into different accounts. Anything you usually do with your money now, you can also do with Direct Deposit. After I sign up for Direct Deposit, do I have to stay with the same bank? No, you can use Direct Deposit at any bank. If you move your account to another bank, you can change your information by logging onto your Payment Profile and make your adjustment. If you choose to enroll in Direct Deposit but subsequently change your mind, you can deactivate the Direct Deposit function by logging into your Payment Profile and unclick the Refund Option box. question: how long does the masters in education take

body.answer:
Ramapo lists two education-related master’s programs, but the pages provided do not say how long either takes. The Master of Arts in Special Education is a 36-credit in-seat cohort program [1]. The Master of Science in Educational Technology is a 34-credit hybrid program [2]. I don’t have verified information about their duration; contact Graduate Admissions.

**Graduate Admissions**: Phone: (201) 684-7270. Email: graduate@ramapo.edu. Location: McBride House. [35]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/graduate/home/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/graduate/home/) [35](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)
